scope.summary: Establish full Argus coverage per Section 13.27 GUI clauses (HBR-VIS): inspect, steer, and screenshot every BodyKit pane headlessly, with a persisted capture matrix that includes archetype edge states (ARCH-A extreme tits, ARCH-F oversized cock erection) so visual regressions on extreme builds are caught mechanically.
acceptance_criteria: Argus inspects the accesskit tree of every BodyKit pane (editor shell, sliders, recipe browser, measurement panel, coupling inspector, pose editor, genital panel, viewport controls) and can steer each control class by author_id headlessly.

The capture matrix enumerates pane x state cells including archetype edge states: ARCH-A slider panel at extreme breast over-range, ARCH-F genital panel at full erection, coupling inspector with a disabled edge, measurement panel mid-solve.
Matrix captures persist as CAP- rows with pane id, author_id path, and state hash correlation; re-running with unchanged state is idempotent.
The renderer console error scan and layout overlap check run per cell and must be clean; failures name the pane and cell.
The matrix run is the HBR-VIS evidence artifact for the BodyKit GUI surface (MT-652 consumes it).

The exact TailorSurfaceDescriptor row MT-634 enumerates every route, pane, control author_id, dynamic entity-key rule, action, state, help anchor, permission, undo policy, receipt, and command binding; wildcard-only evidence is rejected.

Applicable blank, loading, populated, stale/conflict, cancelled, failed, retry, permission, keyboard/focus, narrow/4K/DPI, overlap/clipping, and no-focus-steal states are covered by the registry-derived Argus matrix.
scope.risk_if_missed: GUI regressions on exactly the extreme states the product exists for (over-range sliders, erection panels) ship unseen because no human clicks through every archetype edge case on every change.

surfaces: BodyKit Argus visual matrix runner and evidence browser

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit workspace and controls

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT must wire the shared internal_diagnostics API for its native, job, device, solver-run, or DCC failure modes with bounded structured evidence.
Long-running, native, or external-process work must register bounded progress and child/process identity with the shared Palmistry watcher; Tailor must not fork a watcher.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: BodyKit GUI must expose or integrate the geometry/morph, joint, weight/rigidity, transfer, skin/material, interlink, Jobs, Problems, history, recovery, and shared-world contracts.
Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.

requirements: Resolve Principal, AuthenticatedSession and AccessSpace before every resource read or mutation.
Use PostgreSQL RLS/FORCE RLS and ResourceBroker-backed artifact/file handles; UI filtering is never the security boundary.
Derived resources preserve the intersection of source access scopes and must not leak existence through counts, search, previews, logs, traces, caches, diagnostics, exports or model context.
